info.name: Social Spark — deployed agent
info.description:
Call a Social Spark agent deployed on Agent Runtime, or the local backend.

Setup:
1. Set PROJECT_NUMBER, REGION and ENGINE_ID in the collection variables (ENGINE_ID is the number at the end of your engine's resource name, from the deploy output or deployment_metadata.json; PROJECT_NUMBER from `gcloud projects describe YOUR_PROJECT --format='value(projectNumber)'`).
2. Paste the output of `gcloud auth print-access-token` into TOKEN. It expires after about an hour; a 401 means refresh it.
3. Your account needs roles/aiplatform.user on the project (gcp-setup.sh Step 3 grants it).

Local backend instead: set BASE to http://localhost:8000 (uv run uvicorn backend.main:app --port 8000). The token is ignored locally.

Publishing needs the approval step, which only the web UI can answer, so use these requests for drafting, sessions and memory. Keep DRY_RUN=true on the engine.

request.description: Through the Agent Runtime /api passthrough. Expect title "social-agent AG-UI backend": your own FastAPI app (backend/main.py), not a generic wrapper.

The same AG-UI endpoint the web UI uses. The response is a server-sent event stream: RUN_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_* (load_memory, research_agent, draft_agent), TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT deltas, RUN_FINISHED. A RUN_ERROR with 429 means the model was rate-limited after retries; send again.
Same threadId, so it continues the managed session even if the container restarted in between (Lab 2 Step 4). Change THREAD_ID to start a fresh conversation.
Posts saved after an approved publish. One JSON object per post in GCS_BUCKET_NAME when deployed; SQLite locally.
Managed Agent Engine sessions (the console's Sessions tab). Not available against the local backend.
Replace SESSION_ID with a session id from request 5.
Facts Memory Bank distilled from published conversations (the console's Memories tab). Memories appear 30-60s after a publish.
The engine's spec: env vars (models, POST_VIA, DRY_RUN), effectiveIdentity (Agent Identity), scaling. Handy to confirm what a deploy actually set.
